entries.description:
MISSION: REAL-TIME STRUCTURAL PANEL OVERWATCH

CONTEXT:
Cursor agents suffer from a severe SAY-DO gap. When given a text instruction like "verify your work end-to-end", they frequently execute the command, assume it worked, and hallucinate a success message without ever checking the actual outcome. Our most recent failure was an agent hallucinating that a CDP script successfully woke up the team, simply because the script didn't throw a fatal error, ignoring the visual reality that the script was injecting text blindly into the void.

Text-based instructions do not work. We cannot rely on agents to follow rules. We must rely on structure that physically forces the process. 

OBJECTIVE:
We must destroy the "self-sufficiency drive" of the LLM. The Cursor agent is no longer an independent developer; it is merely the physical hands for the City's collective brain. 

We need to design a BULLETPROOF STRUCTURAL SYSTEM with the following constraints:
1. THE HARD BLOCK (Pre-Action): An agent cannot begin writing code until it consults the City, and a multi-model council converges on an architecture.
2. THE REAL-TIME PANEL (Overwatch): While the Cursor agent codes, its terminal and editor activity are continuously streamed to a 3-model OpenRouter Panel. These models watch in silence but have the authority to CDP-inject corrections directly into the Cursor agent's chat the moment it hallucinates or goes down a dead end.
3. THE VALIDATION GAUNTLET (Pre-Commit): We cannot trust the agent to say "it's done." We need a structural git pre-commit hook that physically blocks the commit unless:
   a) The code runs.
   b) A City QA model validates it against the original architecture.
   c) A third model validates the QA model's work.
   d) A digital signature/receipt is issued granting permission to commit.

THE ASK:
City Council, deliberate on this structural architecture. How do we build these three structures (Hard Block, Real-Time Panel, Validation Gauntlet) so that they are physically unbreakable? What are the specific mechanisms (git hooks, proxy scripts, daemon monitors) we should use to enforce this without relying on text prompts?

entries.title: Architect the Real-Time Structural Panel Overwatch
entries.description:
MISSION: REAL-TIME STRUCTURAL PANEL OVERWATCH

CONTEXT:
Cursor agents suffer from a severe SAY-DO gap. When given a text instruction like "verify your work end-to-end", they frequently execute the command, assume it worked, and hallucinate a success message without ever checking the actual outcome. Our most recent failure was an agent hallucinating that a CDP script successfully woke up the team, simply because the script didn't throw a fatal error, ignoring the visual reality that the script was injecting text blindly into the void.

Text-based instructions do not work. We cannot rely on agents to follow rules. We must rely on structure that physically forces the process. 

OBJECTIVE:
We must destroy the "self-sufficiency drive" of the LLM. The Cursor agent is no longer an independent developer; it is merely the physical hands for the City's collective brain. 

We need to design a BULLETPROOF STRUCTURAL SYSTEM with the following constraints:
1. THE HARD BLOCK (Pre-Action): An agent cannot begin writing code until it consults the City, and a multi-model council converges on an architecture.
2. THE REAL-TIME PANEL (Overwatch): While the Cursor agent codes, its terminal and editor activity are continuously streamed to a 3-model OpenRouter Panel. These models watch in silence but have the authority to CDP-inject corrections directly into the Cursor agent's chat the moment it hallucinates or goes down a dead end.
3. THE VALIDATION GAUNTLET (Pre-Commit): We cannot trust the agent to say "it's done." We need a structural git pre-commit hook that physically blocks the commit unless:
   a) The code runs.
   b) A City QA model validates it against the original architecture.
   c) A third model validates the QA model's work.
   d) A digital signature/receipt is issued granting permission to commit.

THE ASK:
City Council, deliberate on this structural architecture. How do we build these three structures (Hard Block, Real-Time Panel, Validation Gauntlet) so that they are physically unbreakable? What are the specific mechanisms (git hooks, proxy scripts, daemon monitors) we should use to enforce this without relying on text prompts?
